subject: ventures/appointment-no-show-analyzer
professional: a salon or medical/dental practice manager who tracks no-show and late-cancel KPIs from the scheduling system; first checks: is the no-show rate's denominator the standard one (no-shows over appointments still scheduled at start time, MGMA-style), are late cancels identified the way the booking system marks them, is lost revenue the scheduled service price (not the amount paid), are small groups kept from being called 'worst', and is the deposit what-if arithmetic right

evidence.correctness: Dumped the built-in sample export (node scratchpad/ns/dump.mjs) and recomputed it with an independent Python csv script (python3 -I indep.py) that shares no code with calc.mjs: 197 counted bookings, 39 no-shows = 19.80%, 3 late cancels (cancelled-at under 24 h before start) = 1.52%, revenue lost $2,430, late-cancel at risk $230, what-if (2660 x 0.30) + (2660 x 0.70 x 0.25) = $1,263.50, x 365/92 = $5,012.80/yr, weekday rates (Thursday 28.1% worst) and all 8 repeat offenders with their dollars (Ben Ortiz 12 / $695 ... Hugo Diaz 2 / $90): every figure matches the tool. Probes on realistic export shapes give wrong numbers (node scratchpad/ns/probe.mjs): (1) a status of 'Late Cancel' with no cancelled-at column gives lateCancels 0, late revenue $0 and the finding 'Late cancellations cannot be told apart', though the booking system has already told them apart; (2) a file whose only money column is 'Amount Paid' is read as the price (alias 'amountpaid'/'paid'), so no-shows (paid 0) give revenue lost $0 with no warning; (3) 10 kept, 2 no-shows, 8 early cancels gives 10.0%, where the MGMA-style rate no-shows/(kept+no-shows) is 16.7%. Arithmetic right, outputs wrong on common inputs: 2.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked end to end on the sample and probes: no-show and late-cancel rates, revenue lost, by weekday/hour/service/lead time, repeat offenders with dollars, deposit what-if with annualisation, small-sample marking (groups under 5 never named worst), service-average then placeholder price, business-cancelled and open bookings excluded and counted, duplicate rows dropped, skipped rows with reasons, CSV download and text summary, delimiter/BOM/UTF-16/date-order handling. All work. The decimal-comma helper crashed every file from 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-19 (comment at calc.mjs:553, test decimal-comma-pipeline.test.mjs), already fixed. served-copy reports no placeholder origin. No stubs or TODOs: 3.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject dir: 63 pass, 0 fail, 0.17 s. Six seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: late window < -> <= caught; fee-on-remaining (1-p) dropped caught; LOW_SAMPLE 5 -> 4 SURVIVED; lead bucket >= 48 -> > 48 SURVIVED; annualise spanDays >= 28 -> > 28 SURVIVED; service-average price s.t/s.n -> s.t/(s.n+1) SURVIVED (the test named for service-average prices only prices a completed row, so the no-show valuation path is never checked). 2 of 6 caught: 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (567 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, all tests. One engine, pure functions, no DOM in calc, CSV formula-injection guard in reportCsv, wall-clock dates documented, input validation returns messages rather than NaN. Defects: summaryText's own worst() (calc.mjs:508) differs from worstOf (needs >=2 groups and > overall) so the text summary can name a 'highest' weekday the findings would not; defaultPrice defaults to 0 so a priceless file reports $0 lost (flagged as placeholder, but zero); ISO 'Z'/offset timestamps are stripped and read as local wall time (calc.mjs:136), so a UTC-stamped export shifts the hour table. Acceptable: 3.
evidence.claims: Checked 8 claims: disclaimer and no-warranty on page and README (page.test.mjs passes and grep confirms); nothing uploaded (grep finds no fetch/sendBeacon/XMLHttpRequest in calc.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html); usage counts local-only and honour DNT/GPC (usage.mjs:34); aliases stated as unverified against real Square/Acuity/Calendly/Vagaro/Fresha/Booksy exports (README, FAQ); default price flagged as placeholder; what-if labelled assumptions not a forecast; small groups not called worst (worstOf, calc.mjs:352); FAQ 'cancellations with no cancelled-at date ... never as late' matches code (that is the defect, not an overclaim). llms.txt links the old github.io URL in source but served-copy rewrites it (source-only). Every claim backed: 3.
evidence.fitness: Walked a salon owner's job with the sample and probes: export, drop, read rate, worst day/hour, repeat offenders, decide on a deposit. Works for an export shaped like the sample. But no real vendor export has ever been run (VENTURE.yaml says so), the systems that mark 'Late Cancel' as a status get no late-cancel figures at all, and an amount-paid column zeroes lost revenue silently. A practice manager comparing to a published benchmark gets a rate deflated by early cancels. 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with practice-management convention (MGMA-style no-show rate = no-shows / appointments still scheduled at start, i.e. kept + no-shows; late cancels tracked as their own rate; lost revenue at the scheduled fee): exclusions of provider-cancelled and open bookings, notice-window late cancels, and scheduled-price valuation are right. Departures: early client cancellations (slots that could be refilled) sit in the no-show denominator, deflating the rate by the cancellation share (10.0% vs 16.7% in the probe) and making it incomparable to benchmarks; explicit 'Late Cancel' statuses ignored; the what-if counts prevented late cancels at full price although the page itself says some late-cancelled slots were rebooked; no benchmark range offered. 2.

(nsLost + lateLost) * (1 - p) * f * c -> (nsLost + lateLost) * f * c

defects.what: A status that already reads 'Late Cancel' / 'Late Cancellation' is mapped to a plain cancellation and, with no cancelled-at column, counted as unknown notice: 0 late cancels, $0 at risk, and the what-if leaves them out; the finding says late cancels 'cannot be told apart' though the booking system marked them
'Paid' and 'Amount Paid' are price aliases, so an export whose money column is the amount paid values every no-show at $0 (revenue lost $0) with no warning

No-show rate denominator includes client cancellations made with notice, unlike the practice-management convention (no-shows / kept + no-shows): 10 kept, 2 no-shows, 8 early cancels reports 10.0% vs 16.7%, so the rate is deflated by the cancellation share and not comparable to benchmarks; the denominator is stated but no conventional rate is offered
4 of 6 seeded mutants survive: small-sample threshold, lead-time boundary, annualisation boundary, and the service-average price used for a no-show (the test named for it only prices a completed row)
summaryText picks 'highest' weekday/hour/service with its own rule (no >=2 groups, no > overall check), so the copied summary can name a worst bucket the findings do not
ISO timestamps with Z or an offset are read as local wall time, so a UTC-stamped export shifts the hour-of-day table by the UTC offset
What-if counts prevented late cancels as kept visits at full price, though the page says some late-cancelled slots are rebooked (double counting the rebooked share)

verdict: A careful, privacy-respecting export analyzer whose arithmetic is right: on its own 197-booking sample an independent Python recomputation reproduces the no-show rate (19.80%), late-cancel rate (1.52%), revenue lost ($2,430), at-risk revenue ($230), the deposit what-if ($1,263.50, $5,012.80 a year), the weekday table and all eight repeat offenders. But it gives wrong numbers on common real-export shapes: an explicit 'Late Cancel' status yields zero late cancels, an 'Amount Paid' column turns lost revenue into $0, and early cancellations deflate the no-show rate against the practice-management convention (10.0% vs 16.7% in a probe). It has never been run on a real vendor export, and 4 of 6 seeded bugs survive the 63 tests. Correctness and verification are 2, so it does not meet the bar; it is finished (completeness 3). Uncommitted fixes in the subject dir address the first two defects and the service-average test gap.
